nl.statement: A finite observational experiment with a categorical confounder. One unit is the triple \(O=(X,A,Y)\) taking values in \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\), where \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(d\ge 2\), \(A\) is a binary treatment and \(Y\) a binary outcome. An observed law \(\mathbb P\) is described by its atom masses \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\), collected into the four-vector \(q_x=(q_{00,x},q_{01,x},q_{10,x},q_{11,x})\) and the table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\); these determine the cell mass \(p_x=\mathbb P(X=x)\), the propensity \(\pi_x=\mathbb P(A=1\mid X=x)\) and the outcome regressions \(\mu_{ax}=E_{\mathbb P}[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) on occupied cells. For a fixed overlap constant \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the class of such laws whose occupied cells satisfy \(\epsilon\le\pi_x\le 1-\epsilon\); the cell masses are otherwise unrestricted and null cells are allowed. The sampling model is \(n\) independent observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) with common law \(\mathbb P\), indexed by \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The estimation target is \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a}\mu_{ax}\), the loss is squared error, and \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) is the infimum over all measurable estimators of the worst-case risk over \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\). The rate scale is \(L_d=\log(ed)\), and \(c_\epsilon,C_\epsilon\) denote the two constants of the frontier. — Encoding: `Obs d := Fin d × Bool × Bool`, `structure DiscreteLaw (d) where pmf : PMF (Obs d)`, `obsLaw P := P.pmf.toMeasure`, `productLaw P n := Measure.pi (fun _ : Fin n => obsLaw P)`. Risk uses `Causalean.Stat.sqRisk` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/MinimaxRisk.lean:180) and the minimax value uses `Causalean.Stat.minimaxValue` (Causalean/Stat/Minimax/MinimaxValue.lean:59) at `E = {f : (Fin n → Obs d) → ℝ // Measurable f}`, `Θ = the class subtype`. ANALOGOUS MODULE (same world, same four-cell overlap cone, different estimand): `CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean:26-198` (`Obs`, `DiscreteLaw`, `jointMass`, `cellVector`, `cellMass`, `armMass`, `propensity`, `outcomeMean`, `Overlap`, `productLaw`, `mse`, `minimaxRisk`) — F2 should mirror that encoding verbatim; it is a sibling CausalSmith run, not an importable curated dependency (no CausalSmith run imports another run's modules), so the definitions are re-declared locally in this run's `Basic.lean`.

A finite binary potential-outcome overlay on the same alphabet. A full-data law \(P\) is a law of \((X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\) with \(X\in[d]\) and \(A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\}\). Its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) is the law of \((X,A,Y)\). Under consistency \(Y=Y(A)\) and armwise conditional exchangeability \(Y(a)\perp A\mid X\), \(P\) carries the causal optimal-treatment value \(V^\star(P)=E_P[\max_{a}E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\). The causal completion class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}\) collects the full-data laws satisfying both causal conditions whose observed margin lies in the overlap class of \(\mathrm{S1}\). — Encoding: `FullObs d := Fin d × Bool × Bool × Bool × Bool`, `structure PotentialLaw (d) where pmf : PMF (FullObs d)`, `observedMarginal Q := ⟨Q.pmf.map (fun z => (z.1, z.2.1, z.2.2.1))⟩`. SEARCH TRACE: grepped `Causalean/PO/` for `Consistency`, `CondIndepCF`, `POSystem`, `POVar` — found `Causalean.PO.Consistency` (Causalean/PO/Assumptions/Consistency.lean:53), `Causalean.PO.POSystem.CondIndepCF` (Causalean/PO/Assumptions/IndepCF.lean:105), `Causalean.PO.Assumptions.ConsistencyLemmas.*`. BYPASS-JUSTIFIED: those are regime-indexed measure-theoretic potential-outcome systems over an abstract `P.Ω` with counterfactual variables and `EventCondExp` conditioning; here every variable is a coordinate of a five-fold finite Bool/Fin product and the whole identification argument is finite summation over atoms, so the regime-indexed API is a strictly different abstraction level and would add a measure-theoretic layer with no mathematical content. The same bypass was taken and accepted in the sibling four-cell run (`CausalSmith/Stat/STAT_DiscreteAteMinimaxLoggap_Research/Basic.lean:1-10, 204-241`), which is the ANALOGOUS MODULE for `PotentialLaw`, `Consistency`, `ConditionalExchangeability`, `poAtom`, `observedMarginal`.

The four-cell analytic cone and the Poissonized pilot/evaluation construction. Write \(\mathcal J=\{(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\}\) with generic coordinate \(\jmath\), and for \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) put \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\). The overlap cone is \(\mathcal C_\epsilon=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\le s_1(u)\le(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), and \(\bar f_\epsilon\) is a globally Lipschitz extension to all of \(\mathbb R_+^4\) of the cell contribution to the target. Fixed universal numerical constants \(H_0>0\), \(0<\kappa<1\) and a cutoff \(D_0\in\mathbb N\) calibrate the Jackson degree \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\) and the one-dimensional order-four Jackson kernel \(J_{K_d}\). An auxiliary count \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\) and independent fair marks \(B_i\in\{0,1\}\) split the included observations into pilot counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and evaluation counts \(N_{\jmath,x}\). The pilot builds a random rectangle \(Q_x\subseteq\mathbb R_+^4\), the kernel builds the tensor polynomial \(P_{x,K_d}\) on \(Q_x\), the centered factorial operator \(U_h(N;z)\) lifts monomials to unbiased statistics of the evaluation counts, and clipping produces the cell estimator \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\). Summing, projecting to \([0,1]\) and Rao--Blackwellizing gives \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}\), which falls back to the empirical-ratio statistic \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) on bounded alphabets. \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) names the (open) sharp-constant derivation route attached to this construction. — Encoding: `Cell := Fin 2 × Fin 2` (so \(\mathcal J\) is `Cell` and \(\jmath\) ranges over it), \(u\) is `Cell → ℝ`, \(Q_x\) is a pair of endpoint functions `Cell → ℝ`, \(P_{x,K_d}\) is `MvPolynomial Cell ℝ`, \(U_h(N;z)\) is a `ℕ → ℝ → ℝ` built from `Nat.descFactorial`. Causalean does NOT contain a Jackson/Fejér kernel: `Causalean/Stat/Nonparametric/SeriesSieve/Jackson.lean` despite its filename contains only `piecewiseTaylorApprox` / `piecewiseTaylor_sup_approx_rate` (piecewise Taylor sieve, not the Jackson convolution kernel) — that is a filename false positive, confirmed by reading its declarations. So the kernel itself is new local construction over reused trig-polynomial and Poisson substrate.

The Poissonized moment-matching lower-bound experiment. \(\Delta_d=\{R\in\mathbb R_+^d:\sum_x R_x=1\}\) is the probability simplex, and \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\) are the two multinomial laws of the normalized two-sample distance experiment. The dense hard submodel is indexed by a contrast vector \(	heta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\) through the equal-mass law \(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) with \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\) and \(\mu_{1x}=(1+	heta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-	heta_x)/2\). For an even degree \(K\), \(E_K=\inf_{\deg p\le K}\sup_{|t|\le1} igl||t|-p(t) igr|\) is the best even-polynomial approximation error of the absolute value, and \(
u_{0,K},
u_{1,K}\) are symmetric probability measures on \([-1,1]\) whose moments agree through degree \(K\) with absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\). Setting \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil 4L_dceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\) and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\), the scaled product priors \(\Pi_{0,n,d},\Pi_{1,n,d}\) on \([-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\) induce the two observation mixtures \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) when the total sample size is an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\). Here \(r\) indexes the exponential likelihood expansion, \(L_{	heta_x}\) is the one-cell Poisson likelihood ratio against \(	heta_x=0\), \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}\) is the separation of the two prior means of the target, and \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\) is the minimax squared risk in that Poissonized experiment. — SEARCH TRACE (concept words: `two point lower bound squared loss`, `total variation testing error`, `chi square tensorization product`, `Poisson depoissonization fixed sample transfer`, `fuzzy hypotheses mixture prior`): Causalean HAS the whole lower-bound plumbing — `Causalean.Stat.tvDist` and `Causalean.Stat.one_sub_tvDist_le_test` (Minimax/TotalVariation.lean:49,107), `Causalean.Stat.half_one_sub_tvDist_le_max_error` (Minimax/LeCam.lean:76), `Causalean.Stat.two_point_lower_bound_of_tvDist_le` / `two_point_lower_bound_of_chiSqDiv_le` / `iid_two_point_lower_bound` (Minimax/MinimaxRisk.lean:74,105,88), `Causalean.Stat.chiSqDiv_prod` and `one_add_chiSqDiv_pi_iid_general` (Minimax/ChiSquared.lean:184,419), and `Causalean.Mathlib.Probability.FiniteMarkedPoissonPartition.poisson_two_n_lower_tail` + `map_canonicalPrefixObservations_restrict_count_ge` (Depoissonization.lean:198,163), which is exactly the `apply a fixed-n estimator to the first n observations of a Pois(2n) sample` transfer used at the end of `lem:dense-moment-matching-lower` and in `thm:all-estimator-lower`. review.note: On every positive-mass covariate cell, cellMass is P(X=x) and propensity is P(A=1|X=x), so the two inequalities exactly express the stated fixed overlap condition.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon}:=\{P:P\text{ is a law of }(X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1))\text{ with }X\in[d],\ A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)\in\{0,1\},\ P\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:consistency}\text{ and }\mathrm{ass:conditional-exchangeability},\text{ and }\operatorname{Obs}(P)\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\}\) for every \(d\geq2\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).

review.note: On the stated domain d ≥ 2 and 0 < ε < 1/2, the structure is exactly the full-data PMF laws satisfying consistency, armwise conditional exchangeability, and overlap of the observed marginal.

nl.statement: \(\mathcal C_\epsilon:=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^4:\epsilon s(u)\leq s_1(u)\leq(1-\epsilon)s(u)\}\), where \(s_a(u)=u_{a0}+u_{a1}\) and \(s(u)=s_0(u)+s_1(u)\).

review.note: Unfolding vectorArmMass and vectorMass gives exactly the nonnegative four-vectors satisfying epsilon*s(u) <= s_1(u) <= (1-epsilon)*s(u), in both directions.

nl.statement: For \(u\in\mathbb R_+^4\) with \(s(u)>0\), define \(g_{a,\epsilon}(u):=s(u)u_{a1}/\max\{s_a(u),\epsilon s(u)\}\) and \(\bar f_\epsilon(u):=\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}g_{a,\epsilon}(u)\); set \(g_{a,\epsilon}(0)=\bar f_\epsilon(0)=0\).

review.note: On the stated nonnegative cone, zero total mass is equivalent to u=0; unfolding armCellValue, vectorMass, and vectorArmMass gives exactly the two displayed arm ratios and their maximum.

nl.statement: \(V^\star(P):=E_P[\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}E_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\).  This is a full-data causal functional; its equality to an observed-law functional is asserted only by \(\mathrm{prop:causal-optimal-value-corollary}\).

review.note: After unfolding poCellMass and poRegression, the sum is exactly the X-marginal expectation of the maximum of the two conditional potential-outcome means; Lean's zero choice on null X-cells is erased by multiplication by zero.

nl.statement: Let \(\overline N_x=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x\}\), \(\overline N_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}\), and \(\overline S_{ax}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=1\}\). Put \(\widehat p_x=\overline N_x/n\), \(\widehat\mu_{ax}=\overline S_{ax}/\overline N_{ax}\) with \(0/0=0\), and \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}=\sum_{x=1}^d\widehat p_x\max_a\widehat\mu_{ax}\).

review.note: The unfolded counts are exactly the cell, arm, and successful-outcome counts, and real division supplies the stated 0/0=0 convention.

nl.statement: For integer \(K_d\geq2\), let \(J_{K_d}(t)=c_{K_d}[\sin(K_dt/2)/\sin(t/2)]^4\) on \([-\pi,\pi]\), with removable values filled continuously and \(c_{K_d}\) chosen so that \(\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}J_{K_d}(t)\,dt=1\). For a rectangle \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\) with center \(b_{\jmath,x}=(\ell_{\jmath,x}+u_{\jmath,x})/2\) and radius \(r_{\jmath,x}=(u_{\jmath,x}-\ell_{\jmath,x})/2\), define \(P_{x,K_d}\) by the even product convolution \(P_{x,K_d}(b_x+r_x\odot\cos\theta)=\int_{[-\pi,\pi]^4}\bar f_\epsilon(b_x+r_x\odot\cos(\theta+t))\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}J_{K_d}(t_{\jmath})\,dt\).

review.note: On the paper domain ε>0, valid nonnegative rectangles, and K≥2, the chosen polynomial evaluates to the normalized order-four product Jackson convolution; the Lean θ−t form equals the paper θ+t form by evenness of the kernel.

nl.statement: Put \(L_d=\log(ed)\), \(m=n/8\), and \(K_d=\max\{2,\lfloor\kappa L_d\rfloor\}\). If \(d<D_0\), return \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\); if \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n<d/L_d\), return \(1/2\). Otherwise draw \(M\sim\operatorname{Pois}(n/4)\), and on \(M\leq n\) mark the first \(M\) observations independently by \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\), producing independent pilot and evaluation counts \(N'_{\jmath,x}\) and \(N_{\jmath,x}\); on \(M>n\), set the randomized output to zero. For \(M\leq n\), let \(c_{\jmath,x}=N'_{\jmath,x}/m\), \(h_{\jmath,x}=H_0\{\sqrt{c_{\jmath,x}L_d/m}+L_d/m\}\), \(\ell_{\jmath,x}=\max\{0,c_{\jmath,x}-h_{\jmath,x}\}\), \(u_{\jmath,x}=c_{\jmath,x}+h_{\jmath,x}\), and \(Q_x=\prod_{\jmath\in\mathcal J}[\ell_{\jmath,x},u_{\jmath,x}]\), with center \(b_x\) and coordinate radii \(r_x\). Expand \(P_{x,K_d}(v)-\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)=\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}((v-b_x)/r_x)^\alpha\). Define \(U_h(N;z)=\sum_{t=0}^h\binom ht(-z)^{h-t}(N)_t/m^t\), \(S_x=(1+\epsilon^{-1})\sum_{\jmath}r_{\jmath,x}\), \(Z_x=\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+\sum_\alpha b_{x,\alpha}\prod_{\jmath}U_{\alpha_{\jmath}}(N_{\jmath,x};b_{\jmath,x})/r_{\jmath,x}^{\alpha_{\jmath}}\), and \(T_x^{\mathrm{JF}}=\Pi_{[\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)-d^{1/4}S_x,\,\bar f_\epsilon(b_x)+d^{1/4}S_x]}(Z_x)\). The randomized statistic is \(\widetilde V=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_xT_x^{\mathrm{JF}})\). In the Jackson branch define the all-data estimator \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}:=E[\widetilde V\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), where the conditional expectation integrates only the displayed auxiliary Poisson count and marks.

review.note: Unfolding the tuning, pilot rectangle, centered factorial lift, cell clipping, randomized statistic, fair-mark law, and Poisson integral reproduces every branch and the stated Rao–Blackwellized estimator.

nl.statement: For \((\mathbf P,\mathbf Q)\in\Delta_d^2\), set \(q_{11,x}=q_{00,x}=P_x/4\) and \(q_{10,x}=q_{01,x}=Q_x/4\), and complete the observed law with conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes, treatment propensity \(1/2\), and consistency.

review.note: The constructed full-data PMF has the four stated observed masses, propensity 1/2, conditionally independent Bernoulli potential outcomes, and consistency, including harmless totalization on null cells.

nl.statement: For a full-data law \(P\), define its observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) by \(\operatorname{Obs}(P)\{(x,a,y)\}=P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\) for \((x,a,y)\in[d]\times\{0,1\}^2\).

review.note: PMF.map under the projection (X,A,Y,Y(0),Y(1)) ↦ (X,A,Y) gives exactly the stated observed marginal atom probabilities.

nl.statement:
\(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) is the set of all laws \(\mathbb P\) on \([d]\times\{0,1\}^2\) for which there are \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_d)\in\Delta_d\), \(\pi_x\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and \(\mu_{ax}\in[0,1]\) satisfying, for every \(x\in[d]\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 q_{a1,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}\mu_{ax},\qquad
 q_{a0,x}=p_x\pi_x^a(1-\pi_x)^{1-a}(1-\mu_{ax}),
\]
where \(q_{ay,x}=\mathbb P(X=x,A=a,Y=y)\).  Thus the support contains at most \(d\) covariate cells; the parameters on a null cell may be chosen arbitrarily within their displayed ranges.

review.note: On the core domains d≥2 and 0<epsilon<1/2, Overlap is equivalent to the displayed existential factorization: canonical conditional parameters work on occupied cells and arbitrary in-range parameters may be chosen on null cells.

nl.statement: For \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) with table \(\mathbf q=(q_x)_{x=1}^d\), define the observed-law optimal-regression functional by \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\Psi(\mathbf q):=\sum_{x=1}^d p_x\max_{a\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{ax}\).  This value is independent of the permitted choice of \(\mu_{ax}\) on cells with \(p_x=0\).

review.note: Unfolding observedOptimalValueRaw yields the stated sum of cell masses times the larger arm regression; overlap makes occupied-cell ratios well-defined and zero cell mass removes dependence on null-cell choices.

nl.statement: \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}:=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\), where the infimum is over all measurable maps from \(([d]\times\{0,1\}^2)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\).

For \(	heta\in[-1/2,1/2]^d\), define \(P_	heta^{\mathrm{dense}}\) by \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+	heta_x)/2\), and \(\mu_{0x}=(1-	heta_x)/2\). Complete the observed law by drawing \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these means, drawing \(A\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the potential outcomes, and setting \(Y=Y(A)\). For even \(K\), let \(E_K=\inf_{p:\deg(p)\leq K}\sup_{t\in[-1,1]}\lvert\lvert tvert-p(t)vert\), and obtain symmetric probability measures \(
u_{0,K}\) and \(
u_{1,K}\) by taking the negative and positive parts of twice a symmetrized norm-one Hahn--Banach measure that annihilates every polynomial of degree at most \(K\) and integrates \(\lvert tvert\) to \(E_K\). Thus their moments agree through degree \(K\) and \(\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{1,K}-\int\lvert tvert\,d
u_{0,K}=2E_K\). Put \(K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}=2\lceil4L_dceil\), \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), and \(a_{n,d}=\sqrt{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}/(64\lambda_{n,d})}\). Let \(\Pi_{0,n,d}\) be the pushforward of \(
u_{0,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\) under the coordinatewise scaling map \(t\mapsto a_{n,d}t\), and define \(\Pi_{1,n,d}\) analogously from \(
u_{1,K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}^{\otimes d}\). Let \(\mathbb M_{0,n,d}\) and \(\mathbb M_{1,n,d}\) be the respective observation mixtures when the total sample size is independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\). review.note: After unfolding the law, approximation error, degree, scaling, product priors, Poisson mixtures, minimax risk, and target mean, the Lean construction records exactly the dense submodel and moment-matched experiment; DenseConstructionDomain supplies only the intrinsic positivity and range conditions needed for the displayed formulas.

nl.statement: \(\mathscr H_\epsilon^{\mathrm{const}}\) is the route that rescales the pilot-local four-cell rectangles by their Poisson noise geometry, optimizes the tensor-polynomial bias--variance functional for \(\bar f_\epsilon\), and dualizes the approximation constraint into moment-matched observed laws in \(\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) for the target \(\Psi(\mathbb P)\).

nl.statement:
Choose the universal cutoff \(D_0\) sufficiently large.  For every \(d\geq D_0\) and \(n>d^2\), the construction in \(\mathrm{def:dense-moment-matching-construction}\) has even degree \(8L_d\leq K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}<8L_d+2\), amplitude \(a_{n,d}^2=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}d/(128n)\leq1/4\), and, for every \(\theta\in[-a_{n,d},a_{n,d}]^d\), an observed margin \(\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) satisfying \(p_x=1/d\), \(\pi_x=1/2\), \(\mu_{1x}=(1+\theta_x)/2\), \(\mu_{0x}=(1-\theta_x)/2\), and \(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}=1/2+(2d)^{-1}\sum_{x=1}^d\lvert\theta_x\rvert\).  The symmetric measures \(\nu_{0,K}\) and \(\nu_{1,K}\) exist for every even \(K\), match moments through degree \(K\), and have absolute-moment gap \(2E_K\) with \(E_K\asymp K^{-1}\).  Consequently \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}=a_{n,d}E_{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}}\asymp a_{n,d}/K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}\).  Writing \(\lambda_{n,d}=2n/d\), the one-cell likelihood identity under \(\theta_x=0\) is \(E_0[L_{\theta_x}L_{\theta_x'}]=\exp(\lambda_{n,d}\theta_x\theta_x')\); hence moment matching and tensorization give
\[
\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb M_{0,n,d},\mathbb M_{1,n,d})
\leq d\left\{\sum_{r=K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}^{\infty}\frac{(\lambda_{n,d}a_{n,d}^2)^r}{r!}\right\}^{1/2}
\leq d\left\{\frac{(e/64)^{K_d^{\mathrm{lb}}+1}}{1-e/64}\right\}^{1/2}\leq\frac1{16}.
\]
Under either product prior, \(\operatorname{Var}[\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P_\theta^{\mathrm{dense}})\}]\leq a_{n,d}^2/(4d)\), and \(D_0\) can be chosen so that each prior assigns probability at most \(1/8\) to a deviation of the target from its prior mean exceeding \(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}}/4\).  The two fuzzy hypotheses therefore imply \(\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_\epsilon(\Delta_{n,d}^{\mathrm{dense}})^2\geq c_\epsilon d/[nK_d^{\mathrm{lb}}]\).  Finally, applying any fixed-sample estimator to the first \(n\) observations whenever an independent \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) total count is at least \(n\) yields \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq\mathfrak R^{\mathrm{Pois}}_{2n,d,\epsilon}-P\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}\geq c_\epsilon d/[n\log(ed)]\), after decreasing \(c_\epsilon\).
